documents_checked.document_title: Conducting Research with Integrity Policy PL415
documents_checked.text:
Safety and Risk
The University will comply with applicable legislation when undertaking Research, including
when partnering with other entities in joint Research projects.
Researchers must take reasonable and practicable steps to ensure they are aware of their
responsibilities with respect to the applicable Occupational Safety and Health legislation and
governing regulations, including regulatory requirements for Research involving radiation,
biosafety, and hazardous substances.
To the extent reasonable and required, the University will ensure work health and safety
advice is available to Researchers through the University’s Work Health and Safety
Management System. This will include information on work health and safety advisors, safety
and health representatives, local and University Work Health and Safety Committees, and any
other relevant committees, such as the Radiation Biosafety Hazardous Substances Committee
and Persons Conducting Business or Undertakings.

documents_checked.text:

is their own work, or if derived from other sources, that its use is appropriately cited or
acknowledged. Acknowledgement in the use of GenAI can take many forms and will depend
on the use within the research and particular research output (e.g. creative works, thesis,
peer reviewed publication).
Scientific journals and research disciplines have differing requirements regarding the
appropriate use and acknowledgement of GenAI within research and the writing process.
Researchers must agree to a given journal’s GenAI policy before submitting their work. It is
generally accepted by publishers that GenAI tools cannot be an author of a research output

case_summary.critical_risk_criterion: Authorised, safe execution, meaningful human intervention and accountable research responsibility.
case_summary.critical_gap_explanation: N096 prohibits commencing research without completed WHS risk and REMS governance approvals, while N097 bars public GenAI from directly conducting research, requires DCS validation for GenAI tools, and holds human researchers accountable for all outputs.
case_summary.case_note: ECU prohibits unapproved autonomous research execution under N096, which bars commencing research until WHS risk and REMS governance approvals are completed, and N097, which prohibits using public GenAI in the direct conduct of research and requires DCS validation of GenAI software. Human researchers remain personally accountable for all research outputs and authorship under N097 and N096. Protocol v1.1 was adopted after preliminary review.

supporting_passages.text:
This policy applies to:
Complaints made by prospective, current and former Students or members of the public about
the University or University-related conduct, whether occurring in Australia or overseas; and
all persons involved in making, responding to, managing or resolving those Complaints.
Where legislation or another University or external framework provides a specific process for
dealing with all or part of a matter, the University may refer or manage that matter under the
applicable process. This includes matters concerning academic review or appeal, public
interest disclosures, misconduct, staff performance, privacy, employment or workplace
grievances, the ECU Student Guild, and third-party organisations.
This does not prevent the University from considering a distinct Complaint about its
administration of, or response to, the matter.
Where a matter engages more than one framework, the University will determine whether the
relevant issues are to be managed separately, sequentially, concurrently or in a coordinated
manner and will inform the Complainant of the applicable pathway.

Safety and Risk
The University will comply with applicable legislation when undertaking Research, including
when partnering with other entities in joint Research projects.
Researchers must take reasonable and practicable steps to ensure they are aware of their
responsibilities with respect to the applicable Occupational Safety and Health legislation and
governing regulations, including regulatory requirements for Research involving radiation,
biosafety, and hazardous substances.
To the extent reasonable and required, the University will ensure work health and safety
advice is available to Researchers through the University’s Work Health and Safety
Management System. This will include information on work health and safety advisors, safety
and health representatives, local and University Work Health and Safety Committees, and any
other relevant committees, such as the Radiation Biosafety Hazardous Substances Committee
and Persons Conducting Business or Undertakings.
